name: llm-prefill-decode-visualizer
description: LLM inference performance math: TTFT, TPOT, walltime for single-turn chat, agentic loops, batched serving, speculative decoding, and KV-cache VRAM. Includes community-measured hardware benchmarks.

endpoints.description: Full OpenAPI 3.1 spec — derive all endpoints from this. Also served under /v1/spec.
Liveness + upstream data freshness: {ok, upstreamFreshness, cacheAge}. Human status page at /status.html.

Run inference math. ?model=singleTurn|speculative|batched|agentic|kvCache|flagged|cost plus parameters. No model param returns a self-describing capability list; dry_run=true validates and echoes parsed inputs without executing math. Every response carries a deterministic id (calc_<12 hex>) replayable via /api/calc/<id>.

Batch mode: {"batch": [up to 50 parameter sets]} (also accepted as "variants" or ?batch=[...] on GET) returns per-index results with per-item ok/error status — one bad scenario does not fail the whole batch. Each item carries its own model field and may set dry_run.
Built-in hardware speed presets (RTX 4090, dual RTX 3090, M3 Ultra, Groq LPU, H100, RPi5) and workload scenarios (RAG, code generation). Feed these into /api/compute.

Community-measured single-stream benchmark runs with normalized model families. No params = hardware summary; ?hardware=&model=&quant=&limit=N filters. Cursor-paginated: {total, items[], has_more, next_cursor}. All data endpoints accept ?snapshot=<id> for reproducible results.

Submit a community benchmark run for review. Required: model, quant, hardware, hwClass (discrete_gpu|unified|cpu_only), prefillTokPerSec, decodeTokPerSec. Server-side sanity bounds + near-duplicate rejection. Returns 202 {submissionId} (queued for manual review, never auto-published) or 400 validation_failed with machine-readable errors.

One-shot machine-readable dump of the full run index (comparable AND batched/non-comparable runs). ?format=json|csv; ?comparable=all|true|false. Each run carries a `comparable` flag; JSON envelope includes dataDictionary.
Aggregated median + IQR speeds per hardware×model group (outlier-resistant). ?groupBy=hardware|model|quant. Cursor-paginated like /api/localmaxxing; sorted by median decode desc.

Ranked answers: ?by=decode&maxParamsB=8&quant=q4_k_m → top rigs for ≤8B models at Q4_K_M. Supports model/hwClass filters and VRAM fit checks. Replayable via /api/calc/<id>?endpoint=best&<same filters>.

Diff two measured runs: ?runA=<id>&runB=<id> → both runs' metrics, per-metric deltas/ratios and a plain-language summary (time metrics normalized to 2048-token prompt / 512-token output). What-if mode: ?mode=whatif&a=<constraints>&b=<constraints> compares two /api/best-style constraint sets and reports options entering/leaving the feasible set plus VRAM headroom changes. Also accepts a POST body {"mode":"whatif","a":{...},"b":{...}}.

Full comparable benchmark dataset as a downloadable file. ?format=csv|json (default csv). CSV is RFC 4180 with a #-comment metadata preamble + data dictionary; JSON carries a structured dataDictionary + runs array.
Auto-generated 1200x630 Open Graph chart PNG from shared-link params (?preset=&prefill=&decode=&scenario=): tok/s bar chart across hardware presets with the shared config highlighted. CDN-cached.

Turn plain-language constraints into the canonical struct: ?q=self-hosted Qwen 27B at Q4 for 10 users under $1500 → {input, constraints, ambiguities, sizingQuery}. Deterministic regex/heuristics (no LLM). sizingQuery is a ready-made /api/sizing query string.

Data-freshness and confidence report for the benchmark dataset: staleness tiers (fresh <90d, aging <1y, stale >=1y), per-group 0-100 confidence, upstream cache state, engine-release warnings. Alias: /api/agent/confidence.json.

One-call hardware sizing recommendation: pass a workload spec (?model=<family>&contextLength=&concurrency=&maxTtftSeconds=&maxTpotMs=&maxVramGb=) and get ranked rigs with required-VRAM math, expected TTFT/TPOT from benchmark medians, sample confidence, and meetsSlo flags.

Versioned dataset snapshot IDs. All data endpoints accept ?snapshot=<id> (and return a snapshot object) for reproducible, citable results. Unknown/expired IDs fall back to current data with snapshot.served: false.

Combined model + KV-cache + context VRAM from just an hfId: ?hfId=meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct&context=65536&quant=q4_k_m → weights GB + KV GB + total, with architecture resolved automatically from the Hugging Face config.
Replay any computation from its deterministic content-hash id: /api/calc/<id>?<original params> re-runs identical math and stamps verified: true. For /api/best results add endpoint=best.
List registered benchmark-watch combos (no secrets returned).

Register a watch: {"model":"Qwen3 32B","hardware":"RTX 4090","quant":"q4_k_m","webhookUrl":"https://…"} → 201 {watchId, secret, rssUrl, matchingExistingRuns}. At least one of model/hardware required; webhookUrl optional (RSS works without it). Secret is shown once and authorizes DELETE.
Unsubscribe: ?id=<watchId>&secret=<secret>.

RSS feed of new matching runs, no registration needed: /api/watch/rss.xml?model=Qwen3+32B&hardware=RTX+4090&quant=q4_k_m. Filters mirror GET /api/localmaxxing; days=N bounds item age (default 30); max 50 items, newest first.

Cron-friendly dispatch pass delivering each webhook watch's unseen matching runs as a watch.new_runs JSON payload, with per-watch delivery status. Also accepts GET. Lock down via the WATCH_DISPATCH_SECRET env var.
Streamable HTTP MCP server (JSON-RPC): initialize, tools/list, tools/call. Manifest at /.well-known/mcp.json.
